brief: My balcony is bright indirect with moderate moisture, and one cat lives in the household. An east-facing balcony with no direct sun but very bright open shade, and a cat who chews absolutely everything.

design.site_summary: An east-facing balcony with bright indirect light and moderate moisture, housing one inquisitive cat.
design.layout_strategy: Upright structural small trees and palms anchor the mid-layer against the back wall, while soft foliage and flowering perennials fill the ground and low containers along the floor where the cat can safely explore.
design.combination_logic: The scheme combines the architectural, slender fronds of the Areca palm with the braided trunk of the Money Tree for vertical and mid-level presence, contrasted against the velvety, textured foliage of African Violets and Friendship Plants at ground level. This creates a lush tropical jungle feel with varied leaf shapes from feathery to broad, maintaining a consistent green and vibrant floral rhythm throughout the seasons.

zones.placement: Against the back east-facing wall, receiving bright indirect light and gentle open shade.

plants.why: Adds height and soft, feathery texture without being toxic to the cat.
plants.role_in_combination: Serves as the main vertical backdrop, contrasting with the heavier trunks of neighboring plants.

plants.why: Provides a sturdy, woody mid-layer structure that is safe for cats.
plants.role_in_combination: Brings trunk structure and bright green canopy foliage to balance the fine fronds of the palm.

maintenance: Water thoroughly when the top two inches of soil feel dry.
Feed with a balanced liquid fertilizer monthly during the growing season.
Wipe leaves gently with a damp cloth to remove dust.

zones.placement: On the balcony floor within easy reach of the cat, enjoying bright indirect light from the open shade.

plants.why: Non-toxic to cats and features delightful textured leaves that satisfy curious paws safely.
plants.role_in_combination: Creates a lush, low carpet of quilted foliage that contrasts in texture with smooth-leaved plants.

plants.why: Safe for cats and adds soft splashes of color at ground level.
plants.role_in_combination: Introduces soft floral accents and fuzzy rosette forms to break up the green foliage monotony.

maintenance: Water from the bottom or carefully at the soil level to avoid wetting the fuzzy leaves.
Deadhead spent flowers regularly to encourage continuous blooming.
Repot every two years in fresh, well-draining potting mix.

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture in all containers using a finger test.
care_instructions.frequency: twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn

care_instructions.task: Apply a diluted liquid houseplant fertilizer to support active growth.
Inspect foliage for dust accumulation and pests like spider mites.

care_cautions: Overwatering the Areca Palm and Money Tree in the back wall containers can lead to root rot due to the shaded, cooler environment of the east balcony.
African Violets in the ground zone can develop crown rot if water is splashed directly onto their fuzzy leaves during watering.
design.pet_safety_note: All plants chosen for this design, including the Friendship Plant and African Violet, are completely non-toxic and safe for the household cat to interact with.
